title: empty("0") is TRUE, so a legitimate qty of 0 is silently forced to 1 despite the ?? default
sourceContent:
<?php
// qty.php - resolve a quantity from request input
function resolveQty($input) {
    // ?? gives 1 when 'qty' is absent or null (but NOT when it is "0").
    $qty = $input['qty'] ?? 1;
    // TRAP: empty("0") is TRUE in PHP, so a legitimate qty of "0"
    // is treated as "not supplied" and silently forced to 1.
    if (empty($qty)) {
        $qty = 1;
    }
    return (int) $qty;
}
notes: Two distinct absence checks with different semantics: ?? only defaults on null/absent (so "0" survives it), but empty() is true for "0"/0/""/[]/false, so the following guard silently rewrites a real 0 to 1. The migration must NOT conflate empty() with null; the (int) cast is a separate truncation edge case.
